slots.hypothesis: The core is the closing-auction minute's share of the day's turnover. It is scale-free, and it is the only new part that the round-2 E slot grew while head 4 sat in the controls. Its family is heads 10 and 11, so the reward puts them in the controls, which also shuts the div(., day_sum(Amt)) liquidity-recoding channel. The 16 seeds all use periphery sets not seen before, and none divides by a dimensional quantity. They fall into five groups: (1) level baselines; (2) nonparametric relativisation: cs_bucket_rank by 30-day Amt, by LogFloatCap, by centroid and by gini, the close-vs-first-minute participation rank difference, and close share minus gini; (3) time structure: 20d minus 120d median, the 120-day ts_rank, and the 60-day z-score; (4) direction: the 20-day mean of close share times last-minute return, and the 20-day ts_corr of close share with daily return; (5) truncation masks, plus one kurtosis cross. Known risk: the SSE closing call auction only started on 2018-08-20.

Tail thickness that is robust to microstructure, plus how lumpy trading is. Round-2 R showed that day_kurt(Ret) loses half its train score inside price or zero-return deciles while valid does not drop. HL2011 explains why: zero returns and bid-ask bounce bias realized moments. An E slot cannot harvest the clean part, because raw kurtosis would sit in the controls and only the conditioning variable's step (the F2 price step) would be rewarded. So this N slot uses the plain reward and changes how tails are measured. Seeds: kurtosis of 5-, 15- and 30-minute returns and of 10-minute VWAP log changes; max-move ratios; 15-minute skew; double-cleaned bucket ranks by price, zero-return ratio and liquidity; a stale-10% exclusion; the 15-minute/1-minute variance ratio and its 20-day median; the 20-day medians of Amt kurtosis and Amt gini; and price tails minus volume tails. Bare day_kurt(Amt) is left out because it has the same skeleton as head 7.

result.summary:
I wrote missions.yaml for seed 806, round 3, and c05_check.py marks it ADMISSIBLE (exit 0). I also appended a round-3 section to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C05/partura/s806/notebook.md.

**Slot a, E.** Core alpha is `div(day_last(Amt), day_sum(Amt))`, the closing-auction share of daily turnover, used for the first time. Its family is heads 10 and 11. Checked locally, all 16 seeds have a new periphery, none matches a library skeleton, and none uses a dimensional denominator. The reason for that last rule: the round-2 hint 'only use denominators that cannot be 0' is what let the GP divide by `day_sum(Amt)` and bring liquidity back in.

**Slot b, N.** It measures tail thickness in a way that resists tick-size and quote noise (coarser sampling, double cleaning, variance ratio, Amt lumpiness), all under the plain reward. I swapped out two of the first-draft seeds before the final check:
- Bare `day_kurt(Amt)` had the same skeleton as head 7, so the library ban would have refused it.
- Four seeds shared one skeleton.

The 5/15/30-minute window ladder is kept on purpose, so that some of those seeds land below the 0.7 rank-correlation ban against head 7.

**Where I departed from the anatomist.** The anatomist recommended a second E slot on `day_kurt(Ret)`. I did not give it one, for two reasons:
- My own pre-registered round-2 rule fired: kurtosis inside price deciles scored 0.4836, below 0.5.
- An E slot cannot capture the clean part of kurtosis. With raw kurtosis in the controls, the shared clean part is removed too, and conditioning seeds only get rewarded for the price-decile step (F2). That step was about zero in valid.

I also followed my rule not to give the centroid core a second E slot, because the liquidity-bucket version scored only +0.21.

**R, 13 variants.**
- Heads 10 and 11: removing the division by daily Amt, the core on its own, and a same-reward comparison of the clean rank difference, the same difference divided by daily Amt, and its liquidity-bucket version.
- Head 7: inside liquidity deciles, and 5- and 15-minute sampling.
- Head 8: stripped versions.
- Head 1: leaf swaps to LogFloatShares and LogTotalCap.

I checked that I would accept every variant if it replaced its head in the library. I left out head 6's window 3→2 variant, because its +0.12 gain is within the noise.

The notebook section covers my updated beliefs, the predictions above, and a scoring of the round-2 predictions: R was 5 right, 5 wrong and 1 half-right, and the source-attribution calls were the ones that were overconfident. I did not read other seeds or groups, ran no servers, and made no commits.
